title: Learning, Fast and Slow: Towards LLMs That Adapt Continually
abstract: arXiv:2605.12484v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are trained for downstream tasks by updating their parameters (e.g., via RL). However, updating model parameters forces them to absorb task-specific information, which can result in catastrophic forgetting and loss of plasticity. In contrast, in-context learning with fixed LLM parameters can cheaply and rapidly adapt to task-specific requirements (e.g., prompt optimization), but cannot by itself typically match the performance gains available through updating LLM parameters. Inspired by how human learning works at multiple time scales (e.g., System 1 vs 2), we propose a fast-slow learning framework for LLMs, instantiated with model parameters as "slow" weights and optimized context as "fast" weights. These fast "weights" can learn from textual feedback to absorb the task-specific information, while allowing slow weights to stay closer to the base model and persist general reasoning behaviors. translated_title: 快与慢学习：迈向能持续适应的大语言模型
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）通常通过更新参数（例如通过强化学习）来针对下游任务进行训练。然而，更新模型参数迫使其吸收任务特定的信息，这可能导致灾难性遗忘和可塑性丧失。相比之下，在固定LLM参数的情况下进行上下文学习可以低成本、快速地适应任务特定需求（例如提示词优化），但其本身通常无法达到通过更新LLM参数所能获得的性能提升。受人类学习在多个时间尺度上运作方式（例如系统1与系统2）的启发，我们提出了一种面向LLM的快-慢学习框架，将模型参数实例化为“慢”权重，将优化后的上下文实例化为“快”权重。这些快速“权重”可以从文本反馈中学习以吸收任务特定的信息，同时让慢权重保持更接近基础模型并持续维持通用推理行为。
tldr: 受人类多时间尺度学习机制启发，提出了一种快-慢学习框架，以模型参数作为“慢”权重、优化上下文作为“快”权重，使大语言模型既能通过文本反馈快速适应特定任务，又能避免灾难性遗忘并保持通用推理能力。
en_tdlr: Inspired by multi-timescale human learning, we propose a fast-slow learning framework for LLMs that treats model parameters as "slow" weights and optimized context as "fast" weights, enabling rapid task-specific adaptation from textual feedback while avoiding catastrophic forgetting and preserving general reasoning abilities.
